A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients who present with symptoms related to their vestibular schwannoma are at higher risk of developing worse hearing and larger tumors.
age at onset and the type of presenting symptom may be used as prognostic parameters.
the younger the age at onset and the more the presenting symptoms are attributable to VS, the more aggressive the tumor growth and the more rapid the progression of the hearing loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age at onset of VS and the type of presenting symptoms have a significant impact on the clinical course of NF2.
patients presenting with non-VS symptoms have a better prognosis compared to patients presenting with VS symptoms, but the difference did not reach statistical significance.
patients with NF2 presenting with VS related presenting symptoms should be considered for more aggressive surgical treatment strategies.
